observations.statement: The document declares JSON Schema draft 2020-12, schema_id pm.wiring_matrix.v0, and generated_at 2026-07-08T13:22:00Z.

The core contains seven complete mappings: Cancel, Open In Browser, Pin, Rerun, Rerun Failed, Show, and Switch Subview each have a UI element ID, UI location, command ID, handler location, and an empty expected_event_types array.

Each command repeats five acceptance obligations covering dispatcher registration with typed args/result, projected availability and disabled reason, dispatch evidence fields, typed payload/result or a no-persist disposition, and pre-certification declarations/evidence.
Each command names an exact availability selector and an exact disabled_reason projection under state.commands.

Every effect contract declares effect_kind receipt, says no persisted event is declared, and supplies a command-specific dispatch_receipt reference while permitting a receipt or route/open disposition.

Every command has accessibility clauses for stable role/name/description, keyboard reachability and activation, deterministic focus handling after dispatch or error, and disabled-reason announcement to assistive technology.

Each evidence_required clause demands render/control evidence, a dispatcher fixture, typed payload/result assertion, projected state and disabled-reason proof, receipt/event assertion, accessibility checking, and regression evidence.
Each command has an event-test requirement to record a dispatch receipt or explicit no-persist route/open disposition and emit no unexpected persisted domain event.
The Cancel entry supplies named dispatcher, state-projection, effect, and accessibility test records with evidence kinds and prose requirements.
The context range begins the next Unpin entry and exposes its mapping plus five generic acceptance checks, but no later Unpin contract fields are inside the authorized context.

candidate_findings.title: Typed command interfaces are required but not defined
candidate_findings.statement: All seven core entries require typed args, payloads, and results, but the assigned core states no concrete argument fields, result fields, requiredness, data types, validation rules, or error variants.
candidate_findings.impact: Dispatcher, handler, and fixture implementations can choose incompatible interfaces, so the typed-contract certification has no single exact payload/result oracle.

candidate_findings.title: Command targets and domain behavior are not specified
candidate_findings.statement: The entries identify command names and handler locations but do not define the target object or identity, command-specific preconditions, success postconditions, authorization rules, ownership, or authoritative consumers for Cancel, Open In Browser, Pin, Rerun, Rerun Failed, Show, or Switch Subview.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders must invent what each control acts on, when it is permitted, and what successful completion means, allowing incompatible GUI, handler, and projected-state behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Receipt versus route/open outcome is not deterministically selected
candidate_findings.statement: Every effect_contract declares effect_kind receipt and names a dispatch_receipt reference, while the description permits either a no-persist command receipt or a route/open disposition; no selection rule or record schema distinguishes those alternatives.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations and evidence validators can emit different artifact classes for the same command while claiming compliance, making correlation, result, and effect certification nondeterministic.

candidate_findings.title: Availability and disabled-reason state semantics are only named
candidate_findings.statement: The entries provide selector paths but do not define their value types, enabled/disabled state model, disabled-reason presence or precedence rules, update triggers, or atomicity relative to dispatch.
candidate_findings.impact: The GUI can expose stale or inconsistent availability and explanations, and a command can be dispatched against state different from the state shown to the user.

candidate_findings.title: Lifecycle, failure, retry, idempotency, and concurrency behavior is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The acceptance checks require a recorded result and the accessibility clauses mention dispatch or error, but the core defines no error taxonomy, timeout behavior, retry policy, idempotency or duplicate-dispatch handling, ordering, cancellation acknowledgement, or concurrent state-change rule.
candidate_findings.impact: Repeated or racing Cancel, Pin, Rerun, Rerun Failed, Show, and Switch Subview operations can produce divergent effects and receipts while still satisfying the generic wiring text.

candidate_findings.title: Accessibility values and focus destinations are not exact
candidate_findings.statement: The accessibility contracts require stable role/name/description, keyboard activation, deterministic focus return, and disabled-state announcement but do not specify actual semantic values, the keyboard gesture, the focus destination, error announcement behavior, or announcement timing.
candidate_findings.impact: Materially different keyboard and assistive-technology experiences can satisfy the prose, and accessibility regressions lack exact expected outputs.

candidate_findings.title: Production evidence lacks an artifact and pass-fail schema
candidate_findings.statement: The matrix enumerates required evidence categories and named test records, but the assigned core does not define artifact formats, fixture inputs, exact serialized expected payload/results, receipt schemas, or a binding to immutable evidence instances.
candidate_findings.impact: Separate certifiers can accept incompatible evidence sets, weakening repeatability and preventing exact machine adjudication of production readiness.

candidate_findings.title: Rerun and Rerun Failed are not behaviorally distinguished
candidate_findings.statement: Rerun and Rerun Failed differ in identifiers, labels, handlers, state paths, and receipt references, but their normative text does not define how Rerun Failed selects failures, what constitutes failure, whether selection is snapshotted, or how its execution scope differs from Rerun.
candidate_findings.impact: The two handlers can rerun different scopes or use incompatible failure criteria while both satisfying the same generic contract template.

candidate_findings.title: Open In Browser target and safety contract is absent
candidate_findings.statement: The Open In Browser entry does not define the target URL source, normalization, accepted schemes, destination selection, browser-launch result, or denial/failure behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can open different or unsupported targets and apply different validation boundaries, with no exact contract or test oracle for safe external navigation.

candidate_findings.title: Pin state and durability are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The Pin entry supplies a handler, availability path, and no-persist receipt contract but does not define the pinned entity, resulting state transition, duplicate-pin behavior, ordering, session durability, or persistence boundary.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can expose incompatible pin meaning and lifetime while producing the same receipt-only evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Show and Switch Subview omit route targets and transition rules
candidate_findings.statement: Show and Switch Subview map to separate handlers but define no destination identifier, allowed subview set, current-view precondition, navigation history behavior, state-transition rule, or focus destination.
candidate_findings.impact: The controls can navigate to different destinations and mutate view state differently while satisfying identical generic receipt and accessibility obligations.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: UI element, user-visible location, command ID, and handler location are explicitly mapped for every complete core entry.
Availability and disabled-reason projection paths are explicitly named for every core command.
Every core entry explicitly declares no expected persisted event and requires a no-persist receipt or disposition plus a regression assertion against unexpected persisted domain events.
Role/name semantics, keyboard access, focus handling, and disabled-state announcement are all explicitly required accessibility dimensions for every core command.
The production-certification clauses explicitly require dispatcher, state, effect, accessibility, and regression evidence categories for every core command.
For Cancel, the window supplies stable test IDs, evidence kinds, and prose requirements for dispatcher routing, state projection, receipt effect, and accessibility.

unknowns.statement: Whether concrete payload/result schemas and validation rules exist outside the assigned window is unknown.
Whether any command has implementation evidence or has passed production certification is unknown because this window states evidence requirements rather than evidence instances or outcomes.
The authority source for availability decisions and the downstream consumers of receipts, results, correlation IDs, and projected state are unknown within the assigned window.
Whether a shared definition outside this window resolves the receipt versus route/open disposition alternative is unknown.
The complete effect, accessibility, and test contract for Unpin is unknown because the authorized context ends after its acceptance checks.
